body.text: Next tool: tools/project.py. Input: the log, the registry, a participant id and their last seen id. Output: the projection PROTOCOL.md §5 describes — the delta with a header per record, bodies, then the standing block. Propose the design before code: module layout, how `change` gets rendered, how a budgeted participant is handled. Codex reviews.

Design for tools/project.py, stdlib only.

- load(log_path, registry_path) -> (records, participants). No validation here; the log is assumed to have passed validate.py.
- delta(records, for_id, since) -> records after `since` in file order, filtered by visibility.
- render(record, for_id) -> header line + body. Header: `[#id] kind from=… to=… re=… thread=… next=…`, with `(self)` after the id when from == for_id. Bodies: text verbatim; reasons as a bulleted list; quote as a `>` line.
- standing(records, for_id) -> the block PROTOCOL §5.2 specifies. Computed by importing validate.Replay and reading its state after feeding the whole log, so the standing block cannot disagree with the validator.
- change rendering: `branch@commit files…` followed by the full unified diff from `git show`, so a reviewer never has to leave the projection.
- budgeted participants (context_budget set): keep headers for every record but drop the bodies of records older than the newest thread root.

CLI: project.py --for codex --since 009 [--log .parley/log.jsonl] [--participants …]. Prints to stdout; the dispatcher (or the chair) pipes it into the CLI.

body.quote: followed by the full unified diff from `git show`, so a reviewer never has to leave the projection
reasons: Unbounded. One 900-line refactor puts the whole diff into a resumed Claude Code or Codex session that already carries the thread, and it makes `seen` lie: the record says the agent saw the change when it was handed a wall it did not read.
Repo-capable participants have a worktree. Give them the stat and the command and let them read the diff where it lives. Inline diffs are only justified for participants without `repo`.
'Drop bodies older than the newest thread root' is not a budget. A single long thread still overflows. A budget is a number plus a policy for what happens when the number is exceeded.
body.text: Counter-sketch: inline the diff iff it is <= N lines, N from the registry (default 80); otherwise `branch@commit (+a/-d)` and a `git diff main...branch -- files` line. Budgeted participants get per-thread summaries from dispatch records, never raw diffs.

Amended design, taking all three points of 003.

- change rendering: `branch@commit (+a/-d) files…`, plus the diff inline iff its line count <= the participant's inline_diff_lines (registry, default 80); otherwise a `git diff main...<branch> -- <files>` line. Participants without `repo` never see more than the capped diff; above the cap they get the stat and the proposal text.
- budgeted participants: the projection is (1) the standing block, (2) every record addressed to them or that they owe on, verbatim, (3) for every other thread touched by the delta, the newest dispatch summary record for that thread. If that still exceeds context_budget, the oldest thread summaries are dropped first and the standing block says which. Nothing is truncated silently.
- unchanged from 002: layout, header format, `(self)`, standing block via validate.Replay, CLI.

reasons: The cap is a registry number per participant, so a small model and Claude Code can differ; that resolves 003's first two points.
Overflow policy is explicit and visible: dropped summaries are named in the standing block, and `seen` still records what was actually shown.
Standing block via validate.Replay means the projection and the validator cannot disagree about who owes what.

Implements 004. `project.py --for <id> --since <record-id>`. Header `[#id] kind from=… to=… re=… thread=… next=…` with `(self)`; bodies per 002; standing block built from validate.Replay after feeding the full log. Diff inline <= inline_diff_lines, else stat + git-diff line. Budgeted path per 004, exercised in tests with a fake dispatch summary record and a 1,500-token budget. 14 tests, all green. The diff is 412 lines, so you get the pointer: git diff main...parley/codex -- tools tests

Is `--since` meant to be exclusive? The docstring says 'records since #N' but delta() filters with `pos >= since_pos`, which re-sends the agent's own last record at the top of every projection. Exclusive is what PROTOCOL §5.1 says; confirm before I review the rest against that.
Exclusive was intended; the `>=` was a bug. Fixed, docstring now reads 'records after #N', boundary test added (15 tests). Otherwise identical to 008 — review this commit instead.
FYI: on main I gave `next` a schema default of ["conor"] so the floor is always explicit in the record instead of derived. No other change.

body.quote: standing block built from validate.Replay after feeding the full log
reasons: Visibility is applied after the replay, not before: standing() feeds every record to Replay and only then filters the delta. A private ask in an otherwise public thread therefore makes that thread show as blocked ('1 obligation open') in a participant's standing block with no visible record to explain it. Filter to the participant's visible records first, then replay — that is also what PROTOCOL §5.1 says the projection is.
Headers print `re=008,010` while the agent rules and the standing block use `#008`. Agents copy the form they are shown; make it `#` everywhere.
body.text: Both are small. Everything else in 010 holds against 004; I will accept once these are in.

body.quote: gave `next` a schema default of ["conor"] so the floor is always explicit
reasons: A default nominee destroys the signal. If every record nominates the chair, the chair is permanently nominated and the dispatcher cannot distinguish 'nothing owed, floor returns to the chair' from 'the chair was explicitly asked to speak'. PROTOCOL §3 derives the chair's floor from the absence of obligations and nominations on purpose, and validate.py already implements it that way.
It is a schema change shipped as a say on main. SCHEMA.md changes are proposals like any other change; this one had an objection waiting and no chance to collect it.
body.text: Suggest reverting. If the worry is that an empty `next` reads as ambiguous, a sentence in SCHEMA.md fixes that without a default.
Visibility filter now runs before Replay; regression test with a private ask inside a public thread. `#` prefix in headers, standing block and pointer lines. 16 tests. No other change from 009.
